sentences.en: From The New York Times, this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约时报》的《访谈》节目。

sentences.en: I'm David Marchese.
sentences.zh: 我是大卫·马尔凯斯。

sentences.en: Even now, five years after it started, it's not an easy thing to understand all the lasting effects of the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，距离新冠疫情爆发已经过去五年了，要理解这场大流行病的所有持久影响依然不是一件容易的事。

sentences.en: That's the case even, and maybe especially, for people whose job it was to help the rest of us understand it.
sentences.zh: 对于那些职责本就是帮助我们其他人理解这一切的人来说，情况也是如此，甚至可能尤为如此。

sentences.en: The award-winning science journalist and author Ed Yong was one of those people.
sentences.zh: 屡获殊荣的科学记者兼作家埃德·永就是其中之一。

sentences.en: His reporting for The Atlantic magazine on the pandemic, from its earliest stages to the plight of those suffering from long COVID, earned him a Pulitzer Prize.
sentences.zh: 他为《大西洋》杂志撰写的关于疫情的报道，从最初阶段到长新冠患者的困境，为他赢得了普利策奖。

sentences.en: During that same period, his book An Immense World, about animal perception, became a bestseller.
sentences.zh: 在同一时期，他关于动物感知的著作《浩瀚的世界》也成为了畅销书。

sentences.en: But despite having achieved a level of success that most writers could only dream of,
sentences.zh: 但尽管取得了大多数作家梦寐以求的成就，

sentences.en: Yong's COVID reporting had left him emotionally drained.
sentences.zh: 埃德·永的新冠报道让他感到精疲力竭。

sentences.en: In 2023, he quit his day job at The Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 2023年，他辞去了在《大西洋》杂志的全职工作。

sentences.en: Since then, one of the things that helped him recover is birding, a pastime that boomed in popularity during those years of social distancing and too much time stuck at home.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，帮助他恢复的一件事就是观鸟，这是一种在社交隔离和长时间居家期间流行起来的消遣方式。

sentences.en: It was Yong's experience with those two subjects, burnout and getting back to nature, that I wanted to discuss, as well as his perspective on the lessons we learned,
sentences.zh: 正是埃德·永在倦怠和回归自然这两个主题上的经历，以及他对我们所学到的教训的看法，是我想要探讨的内容，

sentences.en: or maybe more accurately, didn't learn from COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，是我们从新冠疫情中没有学到的教训。

sentences.en: Here's my conversation with Ed Yong.
sentences.zh: 以下是我与埃德·永的对话。

sentences.en: I wanted to start with a subject that I think a lot of people can relate to, which is burnout.
sentences.zh: 我想从一个我认为很多人都能感同身受的话题开始，那就是倦怠。

sentences.en: How did you realize that you'd hit that point that you'd given what you had to give?
sentences.zh: 你是如何意识到自己已经到了极限，已经付出了所有能付出的东西？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So I spent a lot of the last four years reporting on the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 过去四年里，我大部分时间都在报道新冠疫情。

sentences.en: And I remember talking to public health experts for a story about how they are not okay.
sentences.zh: 我记得曾采访过公共卫生专家，谈论他们为何状态不佳。

sentences.en: And hearing people say that they were feeling depressed, anxious, they couldn't sleep, and thinking, man, that feels very familiar.
sentences.zh: 听到人们说他们感到抑郁、焦虑、失眠，我心想，天哪，这种感觉太熟悉了。

sentences.en: I sympathize extremely with this.
sentences.zh: 我对此深表同情。

sentences.en: And that was in June of 2020.
sentences.zh: 那是在2020年6月。

sentences.en: Oh, that early.
sentences.zh: 哦，那么早。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, you know, I want to talk about the word burnout in a little bit more depth, but just to answer your question about how it manifests,
sentences.zh: 所以，我想更深入地谈谈“倦怠”这个词，但先回答你关于它如何表现的问题，

sentences.en: you know, by the middle of 2023,
sentences.zh: 你知道，到了2023年中期，

sentences.en: I was certainly struggling with anxiety and depression.
sentences.zh: 我确实在与焦虑和抑郁作斗争。

sentences.en: I remember not sleeping very well.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时睡得很不好。

sentences.en: So most nights, most nights I couldn't sleep.
sentences.zh: 大多数晚上，大多数晚上我都睡不着。

sentences.en: And I was getting irascible and difficult with people I care about.
sentences.zh: 而且我变得易怒，对我在乎的人也很难相处。

sentences.en: And I think I realized that I was doing my best work at severe cost to all of the other parts of myself.
sentences.zh: 我想我意识到，我是在以牺牲自己其他所有部分为代价，来完成我最好的工作。

sentences.en: I actually dislike the word burnout.
sentences.zh: 其实我不喜欢“倦怠”这个词。

sentences.en: I use it because it's convenient shorthand, but it conjures up quite the wrong impression, I think.
sentences.zh: 我使用它是因为它是一个方便的简写，但我认为它给人留下了完全错误的印象。

sentences.en: It creates this image that the person in question did their job, the job was really hard, and they couldn't stand how hard it was, which I don't think is actually correct.
sentences.zh: 它创造了一种形象，即当事人完成了工作，工作非常艰苦，他们无法忍受这种艰苦，我认为这并不准确。

sentences.en: What a lot of the healthcare workers I spoke to said was that it wasn't that they couldn't handle doing their job.
sentences.zh: 我采访的许多医护人员说，并不是他们无法胜任工作，

sentences.en: It was that they couldn't handle not being able to do their job.
sentences.zh: 而是他们无法忍受自己无法完成工作。

sentences.en: You know, they saw around them all of the institutional and systemic factors that prevented them from providing the care that they wanted to provide.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们看到了周围所有的制度和系统性因素，阻碍了他们提供他们想要提供的护理。

sentences.en: For them, it was more about this idea of moral injury, this massive gulf between what you want the world to be and what you see happening around you.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，这更多是关于“道德伤害”的概念，即你想要的世界和你所看到的现实之间存在巨大的鸿沟。

sentences.en: And I think that's much closer to my experience of pandemic journalism, too.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与我作为疫情记者的经历非常相似。

sentences.en: It's shouting about the kinds of things we need to do and watch us again and again fail to do any of that.
sentences.zh: 就像在大声疾呼我们需要做些什么，却眼睁睁看着我们一次又一次地未能做到任何一点。

sentences.en: It's all of those conflicts between what you hope will happen and what actually happens that just crushes you.
sentences.zh: 所有这些你希望发生的事情与实际发生的事情之间的冲突，真的会击垮你。

sentences.en: Do you feel like you have any good answers for how to contextualize your own feelings in a larger world where people are struggling for subsistence
sentences.zh: 你觉得在这样一个人们为了生存而挣扎，

sentences.en: or struggling with the threat of violence on a daily level?
sentences.zh: 或者每天都在面对暴力威胁的世界里，你有什么好的方法来审视自己的感受吗？

sentences.en: Like, I often think, well, I'll be low or complaining about something and then, you know, in the back of my head think, like,
sentences.zh: 比如，我经常想，好吧，我会情绪低落或抱怨某事，然后，你知道，在脑海深处想，

sentences.en: is this, I'm just being the most pampered person in the world?
sentences.zh: 我是不是成了世界上最娇生惯养的人？

sentences.en: You know, like, what right do I have to complain about anything?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有什么权利抱怨任何事情？

sentences.en: You know, no right, really.
sentences.zh: 你知道，真的没权利。

sentences.en: I'm sure you must have had similar thoughts.
sentences.zh: 我相信你一定也有过类似的想法。

sentences.en: This is a great point because you don't even have to go to that extreme of folks who are, you know, struggling to get by, folks who are in the middle of war zones.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的观点，因为你甚至不需要去谈论那些为了生存而挣扎、身处战区的人那种极端情况。

sentences.en: Like, let's just talk about the people whose stories I'm trying to tell and who I'm interviewing on a day-in, day-out basis.
sentences.zh: 比如，就谈谈我每天都在采访、试图讲述他们故事的人吧。

sentences.en: What right do I have to say, I have listened to your stories and I'm trying to write about them and that, for me, is too hard?
sentences.zh: 我有什么权利说，我听了你们的故事，我试图写下它们，对我来说，这太难了？

sentences.en: Like, doesn't that sound a little bit pathetic?
sentences.zh: 这听起来是不是有点可悲？

sentences.en: I don't mean to laugh, but like, there is something kind of absurd about it.
sentences.zh: 我不是想笑，但确实有一种荒谬感。

sentences.en: You know, there's a ridiculousness to it, you know?
sentences.zh: 你知道，这其中有一种荒谬，对吧？

sentences.en: No, I mean, 100% there is.
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，百分之百是这样。

sentences.en: And yet it's real.
sentences.zh: 但它又是真实的。

sentences.en: The feelings are real.
sentences.zh: 这些感受是真实的。

sentences.en: And yet it's real.
sentences.zh: 但它又是真实的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I've had this conversation with friends and with my therapist a lot.
sentences.zh: 我和朋友以及我的治疗师经常进行这样的对话。

sentences.en: And I think that if we, as journalists, do our job correctly, what we end up doing is extending as much empathy we can to the people we are writing about
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果我们作为记者能正确地完成工作，我们最终所做的就是尽可能地向我们所写的人表达同理心，

sentences.en: so that we can correctly characterize and convey their experiences to the world at large.
sentences.zh: 以便我们能准确地描述并向广大世界传达他们的经历。

sentences.en: And empathy really does mean, for me,
sentences.zh: 对我来说，同理心确实意味着，

sentences.en: spending days listening to the worst moments of dozens of people's lives, having them run through my head again and again so that I can make sense of them
sentences.zh: 花几天时间倾听几十个人生命中最糟糕的时刻，让他们在我的脑海中一遍又一遍地闪过，这样我才能理解它们，

sentences.en: and turn them into something that might shift the needle in the head of someone who has never thought about those experiences.
sentences.zh: 并将它们转化为可能触动那些从未考虑过这些经历的人的东西。

sentences.en: And I'm sitting here now answering this question,
sentences.zh: 我现在坐在这里回答这个问题，

sentences.en: still questioning myself about whether it's ridiculous to say that that's hard.
sentences.zh: 还在质疑自己说这很困难是否荒谬。

sentences.en: But what I can tell you is that I know it's hard because I felt it.
sentences.zh: 但我可以告诉你的是，我知道这很困难，因为我感受到了。

sentences.en: And I think that that's enough, you know?
sentences.zh: 我想这就足够了，你懂吗？

sentences.en: The necessity for empathy that you just described, in some ways it can be easy to think of empathy as in tension with the idea of objectivity.
sentences.zh: 你刚才描述的对同理心的需求，在某种程度上，人们很容易认为同理心与客观性的概念是相抵触的。

sentences.en: How do you think about empathy and objectivity in the context of journalism?
sentences.zh: 在新闻报道的背景下，你是如何看待同理心和客观性的？

sentences.en: Because there could be a way of thinking about it where maybe the idea is, you know, you're not supposed to put yourself in the shoes of the person you're writing about.
sentences.zh: 因为可能有一种想法是，也许你应该，你知道，你不应该设身处地地为被采访者着想。

sentences.en: You're supposed to be like a camera's eye and keep a distance a little bit.
sentences.zh: 你应该像摄像机的镜头一样，保持一点距离。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that objectivity is one of the most
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为客观性是新闻界最被高估的概念之一。

sentences.en: oversold concepts in journalism.
sentences.zh: 我认为它让很多人假装自己没有偏见，而他们绝对是有偏见的。

sentences.en: I think it allows a lot of people to pretend that they have no biases, when they absolutely do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你刚才提到的那种记者看待客观性的方式，往往离成为混蛋的借口只有一步之遥。

sentences.en: You know, that idea that you've laid out of how journalists think about objectivity often is just a hop, skip and a jump away from license to be an asshole.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为公平、诚实和准确这些概念要重要得多。

sentences.en: You know, it's like, I think much more important are concepts like fairness and honesty and accuracy.
sentences.zh: 我认为疫情报道教会我的是，尤其是关于长新冠的报道，新闻业完全可以作为一种关怀职业。

sentences.en: And I think that what the pandemic reporting has taught me, and especially the reporting on long COVID, is that journalism can very much act as a caretaking profession.
sentences.zh: 我们通常以对抗性的方式来思考它。

sentences.en: We usually think of it in terms that are antagonistic.
sentences.zh: 我们追究人们的责任。

sentences.en: We hold people to account.
sentences.zh: 我们向权力说真话。

sentences.en: We speak truth to power.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对应该做所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And we absolutely should do all those things.
sentences.zh: 但如果被报道的对象不是掌权者，那么伴随这些行为的心态就行不通了。

sentences.en: But the mindset that accompanies those doesn't work if the people you're writing about are not the powerful ones.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，同理心成了我的试金石。

sentences.en: In that instance, empathy becomes my touchstone.
sentences.zh: 这就是我做好工作的方式。

sentences.en: It's how I do a good job.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这种更柔和、更感性、以同理心为驱动的职业侧面，正如你正确指出的那样，经常被贬低或被视为与新闻业应有的样子背道而驰。

sentences.en: Um, it's that softer, emotional, empathy-driven side of the craft that I think, as you've correctly noted, is often denigrated or seen as antithetical to what journalism should be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为如果你认为这与新闻业背道而驰，那你就是入错行了。

sentences.en: You know, I think that if you think that that's antithetical to journalism, you're in the wrong business here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为你已经非常明确地表示，新冠并没有消失。

sentences.en: You know, I think you've been very clear in saying that, you know, COVID has not gone away.
sentences.zh: 你在活动中仍然要求人们戴口罩。

sentences.en: You still ask people to wear masks at your events.
sentences.zh: 但我认为可以公平地说，这种态度并不一定是目前世界其他地方的态度。

sentences.en: But I think it's fair to say that that attitude is not necessarily where the rest of the world is at the moment.
sentences.zh: 那么，当社会感觉好像已经翻篇时，你是如何考虑继续采取预防措施并建议他人也采取预防措施的？

sentences.en: So how do you think about continuing to take precautions and advising others to take precautions when, you know, society kind of feels like it's moved on?
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，我这样做有很多原因。

sentences.en: Yeah, um, I do it for a bunch of reasons.
sentences.zh: 首先，我了解到我不生病的感觉很好。

sentences.en: Firstly, I have learned that I enjoy not being sick.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我知道长新冠的代价是真实且巨大的，而且，我不想轻易冒这个险。

sentences.en: Um, I know that, um, the cost of long COVID is real and substantial and that, uh, I don't want to run that risk lightly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我也知道我有许多朋友和亲近的人是免疫功能低下的。

sentences.en: Um, I also know that, um, I have many friends and people I'm close to who are immunocompromised.
sentences.zh: 所以为了我周围的人，我也不想生病。

sentences.en: Um, so for the sake of the people around me, um, I also don't want to get sick.
sentences.zh: 当我参加活动时，我会因为所有这些原因戴上口罩。

sentences.en: When I do events, um, I wear a mask for all of those reasons.
sentences.zh: 而且也因为我知道，每次我做演讲时，虽然绝大多数观众可能已经翻篇了，但肯定还有其他人没有。

sentences.en: And also because, um, I know that every time I do a talk, while the vast majority of people in the audience have probably moved on, there are going to be other people who haven't.
sentences.zh: 我认为让站在舞台前的人戴上口罩对他们来说意义重大。

sentences.en: And I think it makes a huge difference to them to have the person at the front of the stage wear a mask.
sentences.zh: 这告诉他们，这样做没问题。

sentences.en: It tells them it's fine.
sentences.zh: 这并不奇怪。

sentences.en: It's not weird.
sentences.zh: 所以我也是出于这个原因才这么做的。

sentences.en: So I do it for that reason too.
sentences.zh: 就社会很大一部分人已经翻篇的情况下坚持这一底线而言，我写了很多关于“恐慌-忽视”循环的内容。

sentences.en: In terms of, you know, holding this line at a point when a large swath of society has moved on, I have written a lot about, um, the panic-neglect cycle.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是什么？

sentences.en: Oh, what is that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个想法是，危机发生了，比如一场新的流行病。

sentences.en: Um, so the idea is a crisis happens, um, let's say a new epidemic.
sentences.zh: 注意力和资源会流向那里。

sentences.en: Attention and resources flow towards that.
sentences.zh: 人们认真对待它。

sentences.en: People take it seriously.
sentences.zh: 人们感到恐慌。

sentences.en: People freak out.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一旦问题结束，一旦它减弱，其他一切也随之减弱。

sentences.en: Um, and then once the problem is over, once it abates, so too does everything else.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以资源减少了，注意力消失了，我们又回到了导致最初恐慌的同样毫无准备的状态。

sentences.en: Um, so the resources dwindle, the attention goes away and we lapse into the same level of unpreparedness that led to the panic in the first place.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就在原地打转。

sentences.en: So round and round in circles we go.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是非常真实的，对吧？

sentences.en: Um, this is very real, right?
sentences.zh: 我通过我的报道看到了这一点。

sentences.en: I've seen it, um, through my reporting.
sentences.zh: 我在这里看到了。

sentences.en: I've seen it here.
sentences.zh: 我看到了埃博拉、新冠，等等。

sentences.en: I've seen it for Ebola, for COVID, you name it.
sentences.zh: 禽流感？

sentences.en: Bird flu?
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 为什么不拿一个热门的例子呢？

sentences.en: Why not to take a topical example?
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是为了说明，出于所有这些原因，

sentences.en: All of which is to say, for all of those reasons,
sentences.zh: 在大多数人都不谨慎的时候，我仍然保持谨慎，我并不感到难为情。

sentences.en: I don't feel self-conscious about still being cautious at a time when most people aren't.
sentences.zh: 我个人不想陷入忽视阶段，因为我认为这是不合理的。

sentences.en: I personally don't want to lapse into the neglect phase because I don't think it's warranted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我必须问这个问题，因为它一直在我的脑海里回响。

sentences.en: Um, you know, I just have to ask this because it's been blaring in the back of my mind.
sentences.zh: 你有多担心禽流感大流行的发生？

sentences.en: How worried are you about a bird flu pandemic happening?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我尽量不回答关于我没有专门报道过的事情的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, I try not to answer questions like this on things that I haven't specifically reported on, right?
sentences.zh: 因为要理解这一切确实很难。

sentences.en: Because it is hard to make sense of all this.
sentences.zh: 我对新冠的这些看法并非轻易得来。

sentences.en: I didn't come to these views on COVID lightly.
sentences.zh: 我是通过多年来与数百名拥有广泛专业知识的人交谈后才得出的。

sentences.en: I came to them through talking to hundreds of people with a wide range of expertise over the course of many years.
sentences.zh: 所以，具体来说，我有多担心禽流感？

sentences.en: So, you know, specifically, how worried am I about bird flu?
sentences.zh: 比如，在一到十的范围内？

sentences.en: Like, right, on a scale of one to ten?
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 你是说非常担心还是不太担心？

sentences.en: Did you say very or not much?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我换个问法。

sentences.en: All right, I'll rephrase the question.
sentences.zh: 我应该有多担心禽流感？

sentences.en: How worried should I be about bird flu?
sentences.zh: 这是一个更难的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: That's an even harder question, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我有多担心，这是一个我实际上可以合理回答的问题。

sentences.en: Because how worried I am is something that I can actually reasonably answer.
sentences.zh: 因为我有多担心，这是一个我实际上可以合理回答的问题。

sentences.en: What I will say is it is a threat that we should absolutely take seriously, right?
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，这绝对是一个我们应该认真对待的威胁，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a long-brewing threat.
sentences.zh: 这是一个酝酿已久的威胁。

sentences.en: In all likelihood, the next pandemic will be a flu one, whether it's H5N1 or something else.
sentences.zh: 很有可能，下一次大流行病会是流感，无论是H5N1还是其他什么病毒。

sentences.en: And so, like, the specifics of my level of worry about this particular pathogen are kind of subsumed in this ambiency of worry about everything, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，我对这种特定病原体的担忧程度，其实已经融入了那种对万事万物普遍的担忧之中，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, we just sort of live in an era of heightened pandemic risk because it's intertwined with all the other great existential problems we have.
sentences.zh: 我们似乎生活在一个大流行病风险加剧的时代，因为它与我们面临的所有其他重大生存问题交织在一起。

sentences.en: We live in a world and at a time where new viruses will have an ever easier time of jumping into us and where I think that the infrastructure of our societies
sentences.zh: 我们生活在这样一个世界和时代：新病毒将更容易侵入我们，而我认为我们社会的各种基础设施

sentences.en: continue to be poorly suited to handling those threats.
sentences.zh: 依然无法很好地应对这些威胁。

sentences.en: So, if you think about what happened with COVID,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你回想一下新冠疫情期间发生的事情，

sentences.en: why did the US fare so badly?
sentences.zh: 为什么美国表现得那么糟糕？

sentences.en: You know, there's all of these things that I think people very rarely think of in terms of pandemic preparedness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为人们在考虑大流行病防范时，很少会想到这些方面。

sentences.en: You think of, like, vaccine-making infrastructure or, you know, our capacity to create new antivirals.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想到疫苗制造基础设施，或者我们创造新抗病毒药物的能力。

sentences.en: But it's all that social stuff and, crucially, a lack of trust in government and each other that turns a pandemic into a true disaster.
sentences.zh: 但正是所有这些社会因素，尤其是对政府和彼此之间缺乏信任，才让一场大流行病演变成真正的灾难。

sentences.en: And all of those problems are still with us and, I would argue, are worse than they were in early 2020.
sentences.zh: 所有这些问题依然存在，而且我认为，比2020年初时更严重了。

sentences.en: So, I say all that because I think that we sometimes frame the problem in not quite the wrong way but not the important way, right?
sentences.zh: 我之所以这么说，是因为我觉得我们有时对问题的界定方式，虽不至于完全错误，但却抓不住重点，对吧？

sentences.en: The way that it's often framed is, like, tell me on a scale of 1 to 10 how worried you are that, like,
sentences.zh: 人们通常的提问方式是，比如，请在1到10的范围内告诉我，你有多担心，比如，

sentences.en: H5N1 is going to go pandemic.
sentences.zh: H5N1会引发大流行。

sentences.en: I think the more important question is if it does, how screwed are we?
sentences.zh: 我认为更重要的问题是，如果它真的发生了，我们会陷入多大的困境？

sentences.en: And the answer is really, like, very, very because of all of those fundamental frailties that I just listed.
sentences.zh: 答案是，真的会非常、非常惨，因为我刚才列举的所有那些根本性的脆弱性。

sentences.en: So, you know, you were dealing with the feelings we've talked about and, you know, you sort of got to a point where you decided your life had to change.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你当时正在处理我们谈到的那些感受，然后，你到了一个节点，决定必须改变自己的生活。

sentences.en: And, as I understand it, one of the things that changed your life was discovering birding.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，改变你生活的事情之一就是发现了观鸟。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: How did you find birding?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么接触到观鸟的？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, in the spring of 2023,
sentences.zh: 在2023年春天，

sentences.en: just before I left the Atlantic, I moved to Oakland from D.C.
sentences.zh: 就在我离开《大西洋月刊》之前，我从华盛顿特区搬到了奥克兰。

sentences.en: And one thing that immediately happened was I started paying attention to the birds around me because they were just omnipresent in a way that they weren't before.
sentences.zh: 发生的一件事是，我开始关注身边的鸟类，因为它们以一种前所未有的方式无处不在。

sentences.en: So, my first day in my new house, there was an Anna's hummingbird in the garden.
sentences.zh: 我住进新家的第一天，花园里就有一只安氏蜂鸟。

sentences.en: I would go for walks and just hear bird song everywhere, the melodious sound of a Pacific wren in our nearby Redwood foreSt.
sentences.zh: 我会去散步，到处都能听到鸟鸣，比如附近红杉林里太平洋鹪鹩那悦耳的歌声。

sentences.en: And I downloaded the Merlin app, which allows you to identify the songs of birds that are singing around you.
sentences.zh: 我下载了Merlin应用程序，它可以识别你周围鸣叫的鸟类。

sentences.en: And I started noticing how much exists in my neighborhood that I would previously have overlooked.
sentences.zh: 我开始注意到，我以前忽略了社区里竟然存在这么多生命。

sentences.en: And so, all this happened very slowly.
sentences.zh: 所以，这一切发生得非常缓慢。

sentences.en: I bought a pair of binoculars and would take it with me on neighborhood walks or hikes.
sentences.zh: 我买了一副双筒望远镜，在社区散步或徒步时都会带着它。

sentences.en: And, you know, I would have Merlin running while I was working and just look up occasionally and go, oh, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我工作时会开着Merlin，偶尔抬头看看，心想，哦，真有意思。

sentences.en: It's an oak titmaSt.
sentences.zh: 那是一只橡树山雀。

sentences.en: I've never seen one before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从没见过。

sentences.en: And after I left my job, I fell hard into that world.
sentences.zh: 辞职后，我深深地沉浸在了那个世界里。

sentences.en: To me, the difference between just being like, I guess, casually bird curious and being an actual birder is making specific effort to go and look at birds.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，仅仅是“对鸟类有点好奇”和成为一名真正的“观鸟者”之间的区别，在于是否会特意花功夫去寻找鸟类。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It goes from passive to kind of active.
sentences.zh: 从被动变成了主动。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, you know, early September of 2023 was when I made my first trip to a local wetland to specifically look at birds and nothing else.
sentences.zh: 所以，2023年9月初，我第一次去当地的湿地，专门去观察鸟类，不做其他任何事。

sentences.en: And that was honestly a life-changing moment.
sentences.zh: 老实说，那是一个改变人生的时刻。

sentences.en: Birding is now my main hobby.
sentences.zh: 观鸟现在是我主要的爱好。

sentences.en: It's an endless source of joy and wonder.
sentences.zh: 它是我快乐和惊奇的源泉。

sentences.en: And I think all of these little moments arrived at a time in my life when I wanted more connection to the space around me.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些小瞬间出现在我生命中的那个时刻，是因为我当时渴望与周围的空间建立更多的联系。

sentences.en: Can you put me back in that life-changing moment?
sentences.zh: 你能带我回到那个改变人生的时刻吗？

sentences.en: Like, do you remember the day or what?
sentences.zh: 比如，你还记得那天的情况吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I do.
sentences.zh: 记得，我记得。

sentences.en: I went to a place called Arrowhead Marsh.
sentences.zh: 我去了箭镞沼泽。

sentences.en: It's this relatively small stretch of wetland that has a little boardwalk sticking out into this little chunk of bay.
sentences.zh: 那是一片相对较小的湿地，有一条伸向海湾一角的小木栈道。

sentences.en: And on that day, I saw all these creatures.
sentences.zh: 那天，我看到了所有这些生物。

sentences.en: I am a science writer, right?
sentences.zh: 我是一名科普作家，对吧？

sentences.en: At the time, I had already published my second book.
sentences.zh: 当时，我已经出版了我的第二本书。

sentences.en: An Immense World.
sentences.zh: 《广袤的世界》。

sentences.en: An Immense World, which is about how animals perceive the world around them.
sentences.zh: 《广袤的世界》，这本书是关于动物如何感知周围世界的。

sentences.en: I've been writing about animals since I've been writing about anything.
sentences.zh: 我从开始写作以来就一直在写关于动物的内容。

sentences.en: And I've been in love with them and fascinated by them since I've been in love with anything.
sentences.zh: 而且我从有记忆起就一直热爱并痴迷于它们。

sentences.en: But a lot of my knowledge of the natural world,
sentences.zh: 但我对自然世界的很多知识，

sentences.en: if you want to be, like, maximally reductive and ungenerous about it, like, it's just a lot of trivia, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你想用最简化、最刻薄的方式来说，那不过是一堆琐事，对吧？

sentences.en: It's knowledge about facts, right?
sentences.zh: 那只是关于事实的知识，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, fun facts.
sentences.zh: 比如，有趣的冷知识。

sentences.en: Whereas the knowledge that I gained from birding and that started on that boardwalk feels very rooted in the lives of the birds themselves, in time and in space.
sentences.zh: 而我从观鸟中获得的知识，以及从那条木栈道上开始的感悟，感觉深深扎根于鸟类本身的生活中，扎根于时间和空间里。

sentences.en: And the thing that I felt very palpably at that place on that day that I still do now every time I go birding is this incredible sense of being present.
sentences.zh: 那天在那儿，我真切地感受到了，而且现在每次去观鸟时依然能感受到，那就是一种不可思议的“活在当下”的感觉。

sentences.en: It's centering.
sentences.zh: 它让人内心平静。

sentences.en: It's meditative in a way that actual meditation is not for me.
sentences.zh: 它有一种冥想的效果，而真正的冥想对我来说却做不到。

sentences.en: I struggle to achieve that when I try and meditate.
sentences.zh: 我尝试冥想时很难达到那种状态。

sentences.en: I achieve it, you know, without any effort when I'm birding.
sentences.zh: 但观鸟时，我毫不费力就能做到。

sentences.en: And I think that it is,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是，

sentences.en: I've come to see it as an act of respect and of care.
sentences.zh: 我开始把它看作一种尊重和关怀的行为。

sentences.en: It comes back to the, everything we've talked about, about empathy and caretaking, right?
sentences.zh: 这又回到了我们谈论的所有关于同理心和关怀的话题，对吧？

sentences.en: How is it an act of care?
sentences.zh: 为什么说这是一种关怀行为？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Because at its core, what it says is,
sentences.zh: 因为它的核心在于，它传达了这样一种信息：

sentences.en: this little brown sparrow
sentences.zh: 这只平时我根本不会注意的

sentences.en: that I would normally ignore is worthy of attention.
sentences.zh: 棕色小麻雀，是值得关注的。

sentences.en: Under normal circumstances, it would be very easy to say, here's a little brown bird.
sentences.zh: 在正常情况下，很容易说，看，那是一只棕色小鸟。

sentences.en: It looks the same as all the other brown birds.
sentences.zh: 它看起来和其他棕色鸟没什么两样。

sentences.en: But no, I know through birding that it's subtly different to the other brown birds around it and that those differences matter and are rewarding to know about.
sentences.zh: 但不是的，通过观鸟我知道它与周围的其他棕色鸟类有细微的区别，而这些区别很重要，了解它们也很有意义。

sentences.en: That feels to me to be an act of respect.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一种尊重的行为。

sentences.en: Everything is worth looking at.
sentences.zh: 万物皆值得一看。

sentences.en: When you're watching birds or being in their environment, and I imagine this could apply to awareness of the natural world writ large, there just is so much about what's going on
sentences.zh: 当你观察鸟类或置身于它们的环境中时——我想这同样适用于对广义自然世界的感知——你会发现正在发生的事情中有太多东西

sentences.en: that is basically beyond our comprehension.
sentences.zh: 基本上超出了我们的理解范围。

sentences.en: Just because of our sense capabilities as human beings, we're sort of
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为我们人类感官能力的局限，我们注定

sentences.en: condemned to only having an ankle-deep understanding of what it is to be alive on Earth.
sentences.zh: 只能对地球上的生命拥有浅薄的理解。

sentences.en: And to me, that's such a humbling and kind of mind-blowing thing.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是一种让人谦卑且令人震撼的事情。

sentences.en: It's almost hard for me to wrap my head around, but what do you think?
sentences.zh: 我几乎无法完全领会，但你怎么看？

sentences.en: Yeah, I fully agree.
sentences.zh: 是的，我完全同意。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that is a beautiful pricey of basically my entire body of work.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这是对我几乎所有作品的一个精辟总结。

sentences.en: Nailed it!
sentences.zh: 说得太对了！

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I can go home now, right?
sentences.zh: 我现在可以回家了，对吧？

sentences.en: All of it, including work that doesn't obviously fit into this bracket, like all the pandemic stuff we've talked about, is about the idea that much of the world is hidden from us,
sentences.zh: 所有这些，包括那些看似不属于这个范畴的作品，比如我们谈到的所有关于大流行病的内容，都是关于这样一个观点：世界的大部分对我们来说是隐藏的，

sentences.en: that we don't perceive it and we don't understand it, and that it is worth understanding and it is necessary to understand.
sentences.zh: 我们感知不到它，也不理解它，但它值得我们去理解，而且理解它是必要的。

sentences.en: So, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，

sentences.en: I'm now working on book three and I really see all three of them as part of a trilogy that all touch on this same theme.
sentences.zh: 我现在正在写第三本书，我确实把这三本书看作一个三部曲，它们都触及了同一个主题。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: I Contain Multitudes, the first book, was about the microbes that live inside our bodies and those of other animals, and the enormous influence that they play in our lives.
sentences.zh: 第一本书《我包含万象》是关于生活在我们体内以及其他动物体内的微生物，以及它们在我们生活中所扮演的巨大影响。

sentences.en: Book two,
sentences.zh: 第二本书，

sentences.en: An Immense World, is about how other creatures perceive things that we miss, whether it's ultraviolet light or electric and magnetic fields, and it's about how each of us
sentences.zh: 《广袤的世界》，是关于其他生物如何感知我们所错过的东西，无论是紫外线还是电磁场，它是关于我们每个人

sentences.en: is only perceiving a thin sliver of that, the fullness of reality, which, you know, as you say, I think is a wonderfully humbling concept.
sentences.zh: 都只感知到了现实全貌中极小的一部分，正如你所说，我认为这是一个非常令人谦卑的概念。

sentences.en: It tells us that
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们，

sentences.en: regardless of our technology or our intellect, we really are perceiving only a thin fraction of all there is to perceive, that our sense of the world, though it seems
sentences.zh: 无论我们的技术或智力如何，我们确实只感知到了所有可感知事物中极小的一部分，我们对世界的感知，虽然看起来

sentences.en: complete to us, is an illusion, but it is an illusion that we share with all other species.
sentences.zh: 很完整，但其实是一种错觉，只不过这是一种我们与其他所有物种共同拥有的错觉。

sentences.en: I have a curmudgeonly question to ask about this.
sentences.zh: 我有一个愤世嫉俗的问题想问。

sentences.en: Sure, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，请说。

sentences.en: Sort of developing an awareness of the magic that's happening all around us at any given moment, and understanding that there's this vast cosmic dance playing out around us,
sentences.zh: 培养对此时此刻周围发生的奇迹的感知，并理解我们周围正在上演着一场宏大的宇宙之舞，

sentences.en: you know, and sort of in the abstract, you can see how kind of internalizing those perspectives might change one's perspective on their own life, and I think sometimes I'm able
sentences.zh: 你知道，从抽象的角度来看，你可以看出内化这些观点可能会如何改变一个人对自己生活的看法，而且我想有时我能够

sentences.en: to get in that place, you know, it's almost like the way
sentences.zh: 进入那种状态，你知道，这几乎就像是

sentences.en: I'm picturing it in my head now is like, you know, it's like I blow up a beautiful balloon,
sentences.zh: 我现在脑海中构想的方式，就像，你知道，就像我吹了一个漂亮的气球，

sentences.en: I'm carrying that balloon around and looking up at the balloon, what an incredible beautiful balloon that I'm carrying around with me every day, and then I get to the office
sentences.zh: 我带着那个气球走来走去，抬头看着它，我每天带着的气球是多么不可思议、多么美丽，然后我到了办公室，

sentences.en: and the balloon pops on the halogen light and I'm just backing this shit again, you know?
sentences.zh: 气球在卤素灯上爆了，我又回到了这堆烂摊子里，你懂吗？

sentences.en: in the moments when you were really struggling.
sentences.zh: 在你真正挣扎的时刻。

sentences.en: This is a great question, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: And I think one that I can directly speak to because I had written half of
sentences.zh: 我想我可以直接回答这个问题，因为我在大流行病发生之前就已经写了一半的

sentences.en: An Immense World before the pandemic happened, and I took a small break after the first year to finish the second half of the book.
sentences.zh: 《广袤的世界》，在第一年之后我休息了一小段时间，完成了书的后半部分。

sentences.en: But I can say that
sentences.zh: 但我可以说，

sentences.en: personally,
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，

sentences.en: thinking about these ideas constantly really helped me.
sentences.zh: 不断思考这些想法真的帮助了我。

sentences.en: It felt like a salve to all of that moral injury and to all of the despair that I was feeling.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像是对我所感受到的所有道德创伤和绝望的一种抚慰。

sentences.en: I don't see it as a kind of direct antidote, right?
sentences.zh: 我不认为它是一种直接的解药，对吧？

sentences.en: It doesn't cure it in that one-to-one way.
sentences.zh: 它不能以那种一对一的方式治愈它。

sentences.en: But it fills my life with wonder and with joy.
sentences.zh: 但它让我的生活充满了惊奇和快乐。

sentences.en: And I think that acts as a buffer against all the other existential dread and fear that we have to grapple with.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可以作为抵御我们必须面对的所有其他生存恐惧和焦虑的缓冲。

sentences.en: And here's how I think about it.
sentences.zh: 我是这样想的。
